subject: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk, termination rights, and liquidated damages
messages:
From: John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Morris <claire.morris@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-14 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about Redwood. Before we lock the PO we need to resolve a couple of key commercial / SLA items for procurement and legal. The main asks from Acme Legal/Procurement:

- Fee-at-risk: a holdback of 20% of the first-year committed fees, to be released quarterly based on met SLAs.
- Termination right: the right to terminate for convenience if availability is below 99.9% for two consecutive months, with penalty-free termination and refund of pre-paid fees for the remainder of the term.
- Liquidated damages: if uptime falls below 99.9% in any month, Acme seeks liquidated damages equal to 15% of monthly fees for that month, cumulative up to 60% of the annual contract value.

I attach our redlines (Acme_procurement_redlines_20260814.pdf). We understand these are aggressive asks; we want to surface them early so we can get to a clean contract.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept any of these? If not, please propose alternative remedies (credits, extended support, SLA credits + enhanced runbook). We would like to have a short call with legal/procurement and your team this week to close.

Deal: RD-38291

Thanks,
John Lawson
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

John — thanks for sending these over and for the clear redlines. I copied Rishi (SE) and Laura (Legal) so we can review the commercial and technical implications quickly.

High level: Redwood does not typically agree to unconditional termination for short-term degradations or large fee-at-risk holds out of the gate. That said, we prioritize high-availability for customers of Acme's scale and are open to a compromise that balances operational evidence and remediation before termination.

Next steps proposal:
- Rishi and I will review the redlines and send a short pragmatic counter-proposal by EOD tomorrow.
- If helpful, we can do a 30-min call with your procurement/legal on Wednesday to walk through the proposed language and the monitoring/evidence approach.

Attachments: redwood_sla_snapshot_20260814.pdf (our baseline SLA wording and monitoring page)

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

John / Vanessa — I went through Acme's redlines and sketched a short technical note on measurement and practical constraints. Summary:

- Availability definition: we measure platform availability from the public API ingress endpoints vs. per-customer edge routing. We exclude scheduled maintenance windows (we have a rolling maintenance policy capped at 4 hours / month).
- Latency vs. availability: Acme's asks mix availability and latency expectations. Liquidated damages tied to small latency changes are risky — better to tie remedies to clear "request success"/"error rate" and sustained availability drops.
- Evidence & monitoring: we recommend mutual monitoring (Redwood's metrics + Acme's synthetic checks) and an on-call escalation timeline.
- Cure period: technical issues often require coordinated fixes; propose a 30-day cure period before termination rights kick in, and allow for an independent review of logs if disputed.

I attached a short technical brief: technical_sla_note_rishi_20260815.pdf.

From an engineering perspective, we are happy to offer enhanced incident support and a runbook integration if that helps reduce risk for Acme.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 11:52:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

John / Vanessa — thanks for the redlines. A few points from Legal:

- Fee-at-risk: Redwood generally does not accept unilateral holdbacks of >10% as a condition precedent to contract execution. If Acme requires a holdback, we can consider a staged escrow arrangement with defined release milestones tied to verified SLA performance.
- Termination: termination for repeated SLA failures is acceptable in principle, but it needs to be limited and conditioned: (i) a defined metric (e.g., monthly availability < 99.5%), (ii) an established cure period (60 days) with remediation steps, and (iii) a cap on damages and clear dispute resolution (arbitration). Unilateral termination without cure or evidence is a non-starter.
- Liquidated damages: we can agree to an SLA credit regime and a capped liquidated damages figure, but not an uncapped percentage of ARR. Proposed cap: the lesser of USD 150,000 or 3 months of fees (whichever is lower), applied after verified failures and subject to offset by SLA credits.

I've prepared a redline response reflecting the above; see attached: legal_redline_response_20260815.docx. Happy to join a call to walk through changes.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

John — thanks for your patience. Attached is a concise compromise for Acme to consider (proposed_terms_summary_20260816.pdf). High level:

- Availability threshold: termination right only after 3 consecutive months with monthly availability < 99.5% (note: lower threshold than your 99.9% ask)
- Cure period: 60 days from notice for Redwood to remediate documented issues; termination only permitted if issues are not cured within that window
- Liquidated damages cap: capped at the lesser of USD 150,000 or 3 months of fees for the given billing period; damages applied only after SLA credits have been exhausted
- Fee-at-risk: we can accept a smaller holdback (10% of first-year fees) to be held in escrow and released quarterly based on mutually-agreed metrics; escrow terms to be documented in addendum
- Optional: enhanced incident support (SLA+ package) at a 25% discount for the first 6 months to reduce operational risk

We think this addresses Acme's need for a meaningful remedy while keeping the commercial exposure bounded and tied to verifiable evidence. Laura and Rishi are available to join the call; proposed times: Wednesday 10a ET or Thursday 2p ET.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: John Lawson <john.lawson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: SLA terms: request for fee-at-risk & termination language

Vanessa / Laura / Rishi — thanks for the quick, thoughtful response and the compromise proposal. The Acme team is comfortable moving forward with the compromise language you outlined, subject to: (1) an updated redline incorporating the escrow mechanics and runbook attachment, and (2) a brief legal call to finalize the cure period and cap language.

We can do Wednesday 10a ET. Please send the redline and DocuSign-ready contract prior to the call. Also please include the operational runbook referenced by Rishi as an attachment in the contract package.

Appreciate the team moving fast — looking forward to closing.

John
